perspective:
**Harold Padilla’s available information:**

- Harold knows Arthur Begum as a police officer and a trusted friend/advisor; he often relies on Arthur for advice and support in stressful situations.
- Harold felt frustrated and anxious because his project team seemed unmotivated and project progress was suffering. He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur.
- Harold told Arthur his team seemed completely unmotivated and that he was at his wit’s end. He heard Arthur suggest understanding what drives each team member individually and having one-on-one conversations.
- Harold admitted he had focused mostly on project goals/deadlines, agreed to try Arthur’s suggestion, thanked him, and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold felt hopeful and relieved, believed Arthur’s advice would help, and decided to implement it in team meetings.
- Harold told his team he wanted quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivated each of them. He heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each person and wanted to make the project a success together.
- Despite implementing Arthur’s advice, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- Harold told Arthur the team still wasn’t responding well and that he was worried. He heard Arthur say there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold said he hadn’t thought of that, agreed to set up another round of meetings, and thanked Arthur.
- Harold became determined and focused, believing there might be underlying team issues he hadn’t addressed. He held one-on-one meetings with team members.
- Harold asked the team to share concerns or problems. He heard Team Member 1 describe tension between a few people affecting work. Harold said he would look into resolving those conflicts and asked if there was anything else. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold said he understood, would see if tasks could be redistributed, and that their well-being mattered.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance. He decided to create a more supportive, open team environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- Harold told the team about these changes. He heard Team Member 1 say it sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree it was good that concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad, urged everyone to work together for project success, and said their input and well-being were crucial.

Harold has no access to hidden/private information beyond what he directly observed, was told, or experienced himself—such as Arthur’s private thoughts beyond his advice, team members’ unspoken motives, or narrator-only context.
